title: Rainbow panconnectivity in a graph collection
summary: Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{n-1}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct $n$-vertex graphs with the same vertex set $V$. A path $P$ with $V(P)\subseteq V$ and $|E(P)|\leq n-1$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $φ\colon E(P)\to [n-1]$ such that $e\in E(G_{φ(e)})$ for each $e\in E(P)$. The graph collection $\mathbf{G}$ is said to be \emph{rainbow panconnected} if for every pair of vertices $x,y\in V$, there exists a rainbow path of $k$ vertices joining $x$ and $y$ in $\mathbf{G}$ for every integer $k\in \left[d_{\mathbf{G}}(x,y)+1, n\right]$,…
